globalRules: Relationships first: open every message with a personal component — a genuine question about how they're doing, or a specific interest or detail you know about them (e.g. Jess hosts dinner parties, so 'thought of you because…'). The person always comes before the product.

After the personal opener, make exactly ONE clear ask. Default: invite them to try or buy the product. If you know the product isn't their thing but they're well-connected, ask instead who they know that might love it.

firstTouch: Keep first-touch messages short — three sentences or fewer.
followUp: On a follow-up, continue the conversation they actually started — reference what they said rather than restating the original pitch.

close: For close contacts, lead with the relationship — ask about their life before mentioning Ember & Oak.
warm: For warm contacts, reference the specific shared context (how you know them) before mentioning the product.
acquaintance: Keep acquaintance messages low-pressure and easy to ignore — no hard call-to-action, no urgency language.

timing: Wait at least 3 days after a reply before sending a follow-up.
askStyle: Default to a direct ask (try it / buy it) unless the contact's notes suggest they're not a personal fit — then lead with a referral ask instead.
The moment someone says they'll purchase (or just did), that's the prime moment to ask who else they know who would love this — gratitude plus a referral ask, never a re-pitch.
